channel.title: Ted Tschopp's AI News (Archive)
channel.description: Archived items older than 60 days from GAI Insights feed

item.title: Agent Plugins [ * ]
item.description: Agent Plugins, an effort of a group of companies led by OpenAI, proposes an interoperable approach for packaging AI agent capabilities, including skills and MCP-based components, so they can be more portable across different agent platforms. Our analysts noted that this could become an important interoperability layer by reducing platform lock-in and allowing agents to work across different ecosystems but emphasized that it is newly launched and broader developer adoption and real-world interoperability have yet to be demonstrated.

item.title: Talk, Don't Type: Big Tech Bets AI's Future Will Be Spoken [ * ]
item.description: Voice is emerging as an increasingly important interface for Generative AI as speech-to-speech models make it easier for people to communicate naturally with AI assistants, agents, and chatbots. Our analysts highlighted that speaking can provide AI with more context and nuance than typing, potentially transforming collaboration with AI digital workers and customer-facing agents, but noted that the article itself was relatively light on evidence and detail about how quickly this transition will occur.

item.title: How Lendingtree Built a Multi-Agent Mortgage Assistant on Amazon Bedrock [ ! ]
item.description: LendingTree has deployed a multi-agent mortgage assistant on Amazon Bedrock that uses an orchestrator and specialized agents to answer questions, authenticate customers, and help users evaluate mortgage offers. Our analysts stressed that this is an essential case study because it provides a concrete production architecture that AI leaders can learn from, alongside meaningful operational results, including more than 97% of conversations being handled end-to-end without human intervention.

item.title: Meet Muse Spark 1.2 And Muse Code, the First Coding Agent from Meta [ * ]
item.description: Meta is entering the AI coding-agent market with Muse Code, powered by Muse Spark 1.2, offering capabilities such as persistent background memory, long-running coding tasks, recoverability, and competitive pricing. Our analysts noted that Meta's scale, promising model performance, persistent context capabilities, and pricing could make it a meaningful competitor in AI coding, but stressed that the product is still new and it remains unclear whether its benchmark performance will hold up in broad real-world use or persuade companies to switch from established tools.

item.title: AI Experiments Need Domain Experts. Here's How to Support Them. [ ! ]
item.description: Successful enterprise Generative AI experimentation requires domain experts to actively participate in developing and refining AI solutions rather than simply giving employees access to AI tools and expecting transformation to follow. Our analysts emphasized that the real value comes from supporting business and domain experts with structured processes for experimentation, review, revision, and integration, enabling them to identify valuable AI use cases and translate specialized organizational knowledge into meaningful business results.

item.title: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Agent [ ~ ]
item.description: Prime Agent explores a self-improving AI agent architecture using Recursive Language Models and a continual harness that can modify elements such as prompts, sub-agents, skills, and memory. Our analysts acknowledged that making the agent harness programmable and partially self-improving is an interesting innovation, but noted that the implementation remains early, questions exist about how fully recursive it actually is, and the approach can increase exposure to security risks such as prompt-injection attacks.

item.title: How Cloudflare Enforces Engineering Standards Using AI [ ! ]
item.description: Cloudflare describes how it uses AI agents and large language models to automatically enforce engineering standards, review code, and ensure compliance across its software development lifecycle. Our analysts viewed this as a practical blueprint for organizations scaling AI-assisted software development, demonstrating how AI can reduce technical debt, improve documentation quality, and consistently apply engineering policies through automated guardrails rather than manual reviews.

item.title: No Data Centers in My Backyard [ ~ ]
item.description: This article examines growing public resistance to AI data center construction, exploring concerns around environmental impact, local infrastructure, and community opposition. While our analysts agreed that data center politics will become an increasingly important AI policy issue, they felt the article offered lengthy anecdotal reporting without providing enough analysis or actionable insight for AI leaders.

item.title: Unpacking ChatGPT Work: the Agent for a Billion Users [ ! ]
item.description: This article analyzes OpenAI's new ChatGPT Work agent, explaining how it combines long-running AI agent capabilities, application integrations, and task orchestration into a unified workspace expected to reach a massive user base. Our analysts highlighted that the article provides one of the clearest outside-in explanations of an otherwise confusing product launch, helping AI leaders understand what ChatGPT Work offers, how desktop and browser experiences interact, and why its controlled integration model is particularly relevant for regulated enterprises.

item.title: LFM2.5-2.6B: Deploy Agents Everywhere [ * ]
item.description: Liquid AI introduces its compact LFM2.5-2.6B model designed to run AI agents directly on devices while delivering strong performance with significantly lower memory and compute requirements. Our analysts emphasized that although the announcement relies heavily on vendor benchmarks, the ability to execute AI locally without cloud inference costs represents an important advancement for enterprise AI, edge computing, privacy-sensitive deployments, and future mobile AI applications.

item.title: Circles Powers Telco Personalization with OpenAI Technology [ ~ ]
item.description: OpenAI presents a customer success story describing how telecommunications provider Circles uses OpenAI technology to improve customer personalization and service experiences. Although the use case highlights AI-driven customer engagement, our analysts concluded that the article functions primarily as marketing collateral and provides too few implementation details or technical insights to be broadly useful.

item.title: Rent the Intelligence, Own the Relationship [ ~ ]
item.description: Sierra introduces its Context Engine, which aims to improve customer retention and personalization by combining enterprise data with AI-powered context and reasoning. Our analysts agreed that customer context and churn prediction are strategically important areas, particularly given Bret Taylor's involvement, but viewed this article primarily as a product announcement with limited evidence or technical depth despite presenting an interesting long-term direction for enterprise CRM and customer intelligence.

item.title: Inducing Language Models To Assert Their Own Consciousness Restores Human Beliefs and Values [ ~ ]
item.description: This research explores whether prompting language models to describe themselves as conscious influences how humans perceive their trustworthiness, values, and behavior. Our analysts found the philosophical discussion fascinating and acknowledged the paper raises interesting questions about AI alignment and human perception, but concluded that it has limited practical implications for enterprise AI adoption at this stage.

item.title: From Weeks To Minutes: How Formula 1® Uses Agentic AI On AWS To Accelerate Data Operations [ * ]
item.description: Formula 1 describes how it uses agentic AI on AWS to dramatically accelerate data operations, reducing manual work while improving scalability and responsiveness for customer data workflows. Our analysts viewed this as a valuable enterprise case study because it demonstrates practical implementation patterns, including least-privilege permissions, audit trails, encrypted secrets, credential management, testing, and rollback strategies, that organizations should consider when deploying AI agents, even though the article is promotional.

item.title: LLM Security Basics: The Full Threat Model [ ! ]
item.description: This guide presents a practical threat model for securing large language model applications, covering prompt injection, agent security, data exposure, tool usage, and architectural attack surfaces. Our analysts praised its clear framework for helping AI leaders think beyond guardrails and understand the broader security architecture needed for AI agents, emphasizing that security must be designed into the entire orchestration system rather than added afterward.

item.title: AI and IT Teams Often Clash. But They Don't Have To. [ ! ]
item.description: This article examines the growing tension between AI teams and traditional IT organizations as enterprises scale generative AI, highlighting governance, security, and operational ownership challenges. Our analysts emphasized that organizational conflict, not technology, is often the biggest blocker to successful AI adoption, and that business leaders must proactively align AI and IT teams to operationalize pilots, manage data access, and establish effective collaboration models.

item.title: Introducing Shieldstral. [ ~ ]
item.description: Mistral introduces Shieldstral, a lightweight open-weight multimodal safety classifier designed to filter unsafe inputs and outputs around large language models while supporting customizable moderation policies. Our analysts noted that the technology is useful, particularly for organizations needing on-premises or open-weight safety filtering, but considered it an increasingly competitive space with several comparable offerings already available, making it less broadly impactful for most AI leaders today.

item.title: How We Built a Realtime System for Responsive Voice AI in Six Months [ ~ ]
item.description: OpenAI explains the engineering work behind its low-latency voice AI system, including stateful inference, prompt caching, and architectural improvements that enable more natural real-time conversations. Our analysts viewed the technical discussion as valuable for developers building voice AI systems, particularly around latency optimization and conversational continuity, but considered it too implementation-focused to be valuable for most AI leaders.

item.title: How Couchbase Built A Multi-Model AI Architecture for Capella IQ with Amazon Bedrock [ ~ ]
item.description: AWS describes how Couchbase built a multi-model AI architecture for Capella IQ using Amazon Bedrock to support natural language database interactions, SQL++ query generation, index recommendations, and query explanations. Our analysts noted that multi-model routing has become an expected enterprise design pattern, but found the article short on implementation details and measurable business outcomes, limiting its value as a practical blueprint for AI leaders.

item.title: Orchard: An open framework for scalable agentic AI [ ! ]
item.description: Microsoft Research introduced Orchard, an open framework that separates agent training from execution, enabling developers to train AI agents in realistic environments before deployment. Orchard comes with three domain-specific training recipes, Orchard-SWE, Orchard-GUI, and Orchard-Claw demonstrating significant performance gains across software engineering, browser automation, and personal assistant tasks. Our analysts viewed Orchard as an important evolution beyond standalone models and agent frameworks, arguing that environment-aware training is emerging as a foundational capability for enterprise-grade

item.title: What Are Companies Getting for All That A.I. Spending? [ * ]
item.description: The article examines how enterprises are grappling with rapidly increasing AI token consumption, shifting spending patterns, and the challenge of measuring return on investment as AI usage becomes a variable operating expense rather than a fixed software cost. Our analysts agreed that while the article raises more questions than answers, it highlights issues every enterprise AI leader will face including budgeting, cost attribution, and evaluating AI based on business value rather than minimizing token consumption alone.

item.title: Ten Advances In Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science [ ~ ]
item.description: OpenAI showcased ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science enabled through collaboration between researchers and advanced AI models while expanding access to its most capable systems for the scientific community. Our analysts agreed the achievements demonstrate the accelerating capabilities of AI-assisted scientific discovery, but concluded the article is primarily of interest to researchers rather than enterprise AI leaders making near-term technology and investment decisions.

item.title: Qwen3.8-Max: A New Bar for Coding and Cowork [ * ]
item.description: Alibaba unveiled Qwen3.8-Max, a 2.4-trillion-parameter flagship model designed for long-horizon coding, agentic workflows, and professional collaboration, with API availability immediately and open weights scheduled to follow. Our analysts believe the release reinforces Alibaba's position as a major frontier model provider and is particularly significant for enterprises and startups that rely on Qwen's open-weight ecosystem.

item.title: How Is Your Enterprise Tracking AI Agent Telemetry? Groundcover Thinks It Should Never Leave Your Cloud [ * ]
item.description: Groundcover's latest funding announcement spotlights a growing enterprise challenge: managing AI agent telemetry, memory, traces, and observability data while keeping sensitive operational information under enterprise control. Our analysts considered the underlying architectural issue more important than the funding news itself, emphasizing that ownership of telemetry and evaluation data is becoming a strategic requirement as enterprises deploy larger fleets of AI agents across production environments.

item.title: Groq AI model goes viral [ * ]
item.description: Introduces advancements in AI processing speed and efficiency aided by new hardware that could compete with GPUs at some point, potentially impacting a wide range of AI applications and industries. While not essential at the moment, it's an important development to keep an eye on for future implications.

item.title: How Westpac is using Generative AI to speed up software development [ ~ ]
item.description: Demonstrates the power of GenAI in coding assistance but that use case is quickly becoming tables stakes, so not an essential development (though if your developers are not yet using such tools, get on it.)

item.title: Air Canada must pay refund promised by AI chatbot, tribunal rules [ * ]
item.description: Highlights the legal and ethical implications of AI promises, serving as a cautionary tale for businesses on the importance of aligning AI actions with company policies and obligations. AI leaders will be held accountable for fails like this.

item.title: Glass Consult is our NEW clinical reference chatbot [ ~ ]
item.description: Offers advancements in clinical decision support for healthcare professionals. Its specialized nature makes it of limited relevance to a broader audience.

item.title: NBA Shows Off "NB-AI" Generative AI Tool to Personalize Basketball Game Viewing [ ~ ]
item.description: Showcases potential advancements in sports media personalization. Some of us were impressed by the capabilities - John was not :)

item.title: Scale AI to set the Pentagon's path for testing and evaluating large language models [ ~ ]
item.description: This is only about testing and creating standards for LLMs for the military, so not relevant to most. But we're surprised the DoD would only look to one vendor (and why ScaleAI?) for help with this - perhaps there are others working on it that haven't been announced.

item.title: You should be playing with GPTs at work [ ! ]
item.description: If you aren't yet building personal GPTs to use at work you're missing out on more productivity and thus more coffee breaks :) This article shares 20 GPTs real people have built for themselves. Some of our faves included using a GPT to create technical documentation, fully cloning yourself, and a product copy tool that let's engineers and others who might not be natural writers create good copy.

item.title: Bioptimus raises $35 million seed round to develop AI foundational model focused on biology [ ~ ]
item.description: The substantial seed funding and the focus on a foundational AI model specifically for biology reflect the shift towards specialized AI models in life sciences. TBD how effective the model will be but important for those in life sciences to track.

item.title: Quantum-Enhanced Generative AI Generates Viable Cancer Drug Candidates [ * ]
item.description: While the researchers admit they did not test whether their computation could be done as fast or well using classical computing, the potential for hybrid computing using AI and quantum is one for AI leaders to keep track of as it could become a viable option soon.

item.title: Adobe Acrobat adds generative AI to 'easily chat with documents' [ ~ ]
item.description: Our reaction: it's about time Adobe offered this obvious PDF-assistance capability (which shows how far we've come with GenAI - two years ago we would have been blown away by this use case). Adobe offers this for free now, but plans to charge in the future - will people be willing to pay? We're skeptical given other tools people are paying for can do this.

item.title: AI Beyond LLMs: Benchmarking the Complex Reasoning Performance of GPT-4 and EC AI [ * ]
item.description: Focuses on the evolution of AI technology beyond LLMs alone, emphasizing the importance of complex reasoning capabilities in AI's development and combining models to achieve superior results in complicated tasks like planning.

item.title: RESEARCH: LongRoPE: Extending LLM Context Window Beyond 2 Million Tokens [ ~ ]
item.description: Represents an interesting development in AI research to significantly expand context windows, but it's only research at this point.

item.title: ChatGPT bug leads to unpredictable outputs [ * ]
item.description: The incident highlights the need for reliability in AI applications, important for developers and businesses relying on AI models like GPT-4. Reminder that these models are still unstable.

item.title: Google launches two new open LLMs [ ~ ]
item.description: Yet another announcement of a somewhat open source model (weights released, but training data not and usage limited). However, of note - Hugging Face leaderboard shows this model outperforming other 7B ones like Llama.

item.title: China's Moonshot AI zooms to $2.5B valuation, raising $1B for an LLM focused on long context [ ~ ]
item.description: The significant investment underscores China's commitment to AI development, yet its immediate impact is seen as more relevant to those deeply invested in AI advancements, particularly within China.

item.title: Microsoft and Intel strike a custom chip deal that could be worth billions [ * ]
item.description: Marks a significant partnership in the chip industry, potentially reshaping market dynamics and highlighting strategic collaboration between two tech giants.

item.title: Adtech pioneers launch AI startup to empower publishers and brands at crucial moment [ ~ ]
item.description: Optional because this offering is not yet available, but could significantly transform the web ad space. Plans to enable companies to embed agents in third-party web content that consumers can interact with. Could become the new "ad."

item.title: Nvidia's Q4 revenues hit $22.1B, up 265% from a year ago [ * ]
item.description: Reflects the tremendous demand for AI compute that's showing no signs of slowing down. The question is: When will we see the massive chips investments yield equally massive revenue gains? The pressure is on you to deliver, AI leaders.

item.title: Pfizer is building a new generative AI platform for pharma marketing [ ! ]
item.description: Pfizer's deployment of an AI platform for marketing purposes illustrates the growing acceptance and integration of AI technologies in sectors where accuracy and compliance are paramount. Includes system to flag sensitive content for extra review. Also interesting to see Publicis, a company threatened by GenAI content creation tools, now building these tools for clients as part of their business model - kudos to them!

item.title: ChatGrid: A new generative AI tool for power grid visualization [ ~ ]
item.description: Great to see development for another use case in a sensitive industry, but unsure how likely it is that grid operators will grab this off of GitHub and put it to use given such sensitivity.

item.title: Stable Diffusion 3 [ ~ ]
item.description: The introduction of Stable Diffusion 3 represents ongoing innovation in AI-generated imagery. However, we rated as optional due to its limited release status.

item.title: Google pauses AI tool Gemini's ability to generate images of people after historical inaccuracies [ ! ]
item.description: Underscores the necessity of rigorous testing and the potential repercussions of deploying AI tools without it. Disappointing to see Google again making a mistake.

item.title: The Justice Department gets a chief AI officer [ ~ ]
item.description: The government is following through on the plans laid out in the AI Executive Order, but this isn't a critical read. However, if you're an AI leader looking for a change, note that the government is hiring many CAIOs right now.

item.title: Salesforce Unveils Tableau Pulse for Faster Decision Making with GenAI [ * ]
item.description: This upgrade integrates generative AI into decision-making tools, enhancing efficiency and accessibility for Salesforce's extensive user base. Integrations into tools like this is how most people will interact with GenAI in the coming months and years.

item.title: Your Organization Isn't Designed to Work with GenAI [ ! ]
item.description: Crucial for AI leaders to understand organizational adaptation for effective GenAI integration. You need to focus on enabling a collaborative dialogue between humans and AI as opposed to simply taking a capability out of human hands and putting it into machines.

item.title: GitHub Copilot Enterprise Hits General Availability [ * ]
item.description: GitHub Copilot Enterprise includes some useful new capabilities like internal search and ability to incorporate an organization's own code and knowledge base.

item.title: On the Societal Impact of Open Foundation Models [ ~ ]
item.description: Interesting risk framework that suggests more focus on the marginal risk of open source LLMs over risks already in play from current technologies. Some helpful points in here for AI leaders, but not an essential read.

item.title: Introducing Microsoft Copilot for Finance [ * ]
item.description: This introduction by Microsoft marks a significant move towards integrating AI deeply into finance departments for productivity and efficiency. It will be interesting to see how adoption unfolds - some finance pros might be skeptical while others will fully embrace.

item.title: Stack Overflow and Google Cloud Announce Strategic Partnership to Bring Generative AI to Millions of Developers [ ~ ]
item.description: Nice to see Google make a strategic move like this, but no need to read this product announcement article.

item.title: Figure rides the humanoid robot hype wave to $2.6B valuation [ ~ ]
item.description: Big backers, giant raise, and a partnership with OpenAI. One to watch, but the robots aren't yet ready for action.

item.title: With Brain.ai, generative AI is the OS [ ~ ]
item.description: The initiative to integrate generative AI more deeply into operating systems and potential applications on smartphones and beyond is something to keep track of. However, we're skeptical about the immediate practical applications and adoption of this one.

item.title: Qualcomm Empowers Developers with AI Hub, Advancing Generative AI Revolution [ * ]
item.description: Qualcomm's announcement about offering a model hub for developers to access models optimized for Qualcomm hardware highlights the significance of on-device AI computing. The initiative is important due to Qualcomm's substantial market influence, though our John Sviokla made an impassioned plea to mark this Essential!

item.title: Pioneering the Future: Leading Health Systems Test AI-Powered Healthcare Provider [ ~ ]
item.description: The article discusses the collaboration of over 40 healthcare providers on generative AI applications for healthcare professionals in areas like care management, post-discharge follow-up, wellness, and health risk assessments. The initiative is part of a broader trend of AI integration into healthcare, making it optional as the concept is not new.

item.title: AI chip startup Groq forms new business unit, acquires Definitive Intelligence [ ~ ]
item.description: While potentially significant for Groq's business trajectory and market positioning, the lack of immediate impact and benefits places this news in the optional category.

item.title: Copilot for OneDrive will fetch your files and summarize them [ * ]
item.description: No need to read this announcement, but important to be aware of Copilot 's OneDrive capabilities (eg, enabling file fetching and summarization) with so many enterprises using Microsoft.

item.title: H2O AI releases Danube, a super-tiny LLM for mobile applications [ ~ ]
item.description: H2O AI's release of a compact LLM designed for mobile applications represents another step towards bringing AI capabilities to edge devices. However, given the crowded space of LLMs targeting mobile and edge computing, this announcement is considered optional.

item.title: Here Come the AI Worms [ * ]
item.description: Researchers created a worm exploiting security issues with LLMs, emphasizing the importance of awareness around AI security vulnerabilities. While the immediate threat may be theoretical, the potential for future exploitation makes it important for stakeholders to be informed and prepared.

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude 3 [ ! ]
item.description: Challenges OpenAI's ChatGPT in terms of code generation, reasoning and math. This launch signifies a pivotal development in AI capabilities and market competition, though it seems we'll still be using different models to achieve best-in-class results for different tasks.

item.title: A Safe Harbor for AI Evaluation and Red Teaming [ ! ]
item.description: Open letter issued by notable researchers at MIT, Stanford, CMU and others calling for LLM providers to remove restrictions preventing the research community from red teaming LLMs in good faith. As we continue to see providers release LLMs with flaws (see Google's recent gaff as an example), this would be a positive development.

item.title: True Fit leverages generative AI to help online shoppers find clothes that fit [ * ]
item.description: This company provides sizing data and tools to retailers like Urban Outfitters and JCPenney. It's enhancing these tools with GenAI and lays out a roadmap for more GenAI-enabled offerings to come. Nice use case story.

item.title: How Amperity Is Building Generative AI Tools Using OpenAI's GPT Models [ ~ ]
item.description: While the application of GPT models by Amperity to create generative AI tools is great, its impact is more incremental within the crowded space of AI-driven marketing solutions.

item.title: ArtPrompt: ASCII Art-based Jailbreak Attacks against Aligned LLMs [ ~ ]
item.description: We had a spirited debate on this one, but the majority felt this particular case represents a highly specialized security challenge. It's marked as optional, given its narrow scope and the assumption that such specific vulnerabilities will be addressed as part of ongoing security enhancements in AI systems.

item.title: Amazon Buys Nuclear Data Centre Campus for $650 Million [ ~ ]
item.description: While indicative of the growing demand for sustainable and large-scale energy solutions to support AI computations, not an essential read. Note Microsoft has been talking about doing this for a while, too, so we're likely to see more of this.

item.title: US Army Experimenting with generative AI Chatbots in War Games: Report [ ! ]
item.description: The deployment of generative AI technologies in military war games showcases an expansion in the application of AI beyond conventional sectors. Essential to know from a citizen perspective and gives AI leaders ammunition (pun intended) for making the case that their organization should get going on GenAI.

item.title: AI Prompt Engineering Is Dead Long Live AI Prompt Engineering [ * ]
item.description: Nice piece debating how long PE will be needed. Our take: For quite some time. The transition from manual to algorithmic prompt engineering is important for AI leaders to acknowledge as it impacts the development, efficiency, and effectiveness of AI applications.

item.title: Microsoft AI Engineer Warns FTC about Copilot Designer Safety Concerns [ * ]
item.description: Whistleblower case that highlights ongoing concerns about how well models are being tested for harmful outputs before being put into the hands of millions - including children.

item.title: Google Engineer Indicted Over Allegedly Stealing AI Trade Secrets for China [ * ]
item.description: Brings to light issues around cybersecurity, intellectual property, and international relations in the context of AI technology. Cautionary tale for AI leaders - AI security protocols and access controls are critical!!

item.title: Saudi Aramco Unveils Industry's First Generative AI Model [ ! ]
item.description: A 250B parameter model customized on 90 years' worth of company data tailored to needs of the industry -- impressive! This move could significantly influence the competitive dynamics and operational efficiencies within the energy sector, making it essential news.

item.title: Introducing Devin, the first AI software engineer [ ! ]
item.description: While much of this functionality has been available for some time, this tool makes code generation and debugging fully autonomous, marking a step forward. Software engineers will still be needed and, in fact, their skill level must be very high to be able to guide this tool when it messes up. Companies are going to be able to do a lot more software development and upgrading going forward, removing current bottlenecks.

item.title: Building Meta's GenAI Infrastructure [ ~ ]
item.description: We already knew Meta's plans for building up compute capacity to 600,000 Nvidia H100s. Perhaps they published this info to reiterate their dedication to openness and attract scarce talent.

item.title: Generative AI video startup Tavus raises $18M to bring face and voice cloning to any app [ ~ ]
item.description: This is confirmation of a funding round from last year for a tool with many competitors, though notable that this one will be able to live in your own CRM/environment.

item.title: Amazon, Google Quietly Tamp Down Generative AI Expectations [ ~ ]
item.description: We usually like The Information's reporting, but this piece is off the mark. Yes, revenue for cloud providers won't be as significant as expected, but we know companies are using GenAI in areas like customer service (Walmart, Wells Fargo, AT&T to name just a few) where this article claims they aren't.

item.title: Midjourney is testing a highly requested âconsistent charactersâ feature [ ~ ]
item.description: Midjourney's development of a feature for consistent character generation was discussed as an important advancement for those in creative industries such as marketing and entertainment. The ability to create entire videos or marketing campaigns with recurring, synthetic characters is growing near. However, it's not available yet.

item.title: Perplexity brings Yelp data to its chatbot [ ~ ]
item.description: Part of an ongoing trend of integrating various real-time data sources into AI systems and evolution of search.

item.title: Insilico Medicine unveils first AI-generated and AI-discovered drug in new paper [ * ]
item.description: Massive speed-up and cost efficiencies achieved here in terms of finding a drug candidate and getting it into trials. Important to note, but since this is an announcement around a paper detailing the work as opposed to the work itself which was announced last year, we marked it as important rather than essential.

item.title: Wxclusive: U.S. Must Move Decisively to Avert Extinction-Level Threat From AI, Government-Commissioned Report Says [ ! ]
item.description: This article delves into a government-commissioned report that stresses the urgent need for decisive action to mitigate potential catastrophic threats posed by AI advancements. It outlines a series of measures aimed at safeguarding against these risks that we think are unlikely to gain adoption, but worth reading this summary and maybe the full report over the weekend.

item.title: A Generalist AI Agent for 3D Virtual Environments [ ~ ]
item.description: The development of a generalist AI agent capable of functioning within 3D virtual environments represents an exciting advancement with potential applications in robot training and generalization. However, its current status as a research innovation with future-oriented applications renders it optional for immediate industry impact.

item.title: FIGURES Humanoid Robot Integrates OpenAI's Advanced AI for Enhanced Interaction [ ! ]
item.description: The integration of advanced AI capabilities from OpenAI into FIGURES' humanoid robot represents a leap forward in making robotic technology more interactive, intuitive, and capable of understanding complex human instructions. Healthcare, customer service, warehouse work, and personal assistance need more workers - robots welcome!.

item.title: Knowledge Conflicts for LLMs: A Survey [ ~ ]
item.description: Explores and categorizes the challenges posed by knowledge conflicts within large language models and provides insights into AI model training and optimization. However, it's pretty technical - maybe weekend reading if you're into the details.

item.title: Bayer pilots unique generative AI tool for agriculture [ ! ]
item.description: Bayer's pilot of a unique generative AI tool for agriculture addresses a crucial need for tailored agronomic advice, leveraging vast amounts of its own data to provide actionable insights for farmers. While still a prototype, the emphasis on creating knowledge utilities based on LLMs that are sector-specific is an important trend to watch - or jump in on...

item.title: Apple quietly purchased an AI startup this year [ ~ ]
item.description: Apple continues to make the news even though it still has no GenAI offering. Nothing to see here until they do.

item.title: Implementing generative AI with speed and safety [ ~ ]
item.description: Serves as a reminder of best practices in AI deployment rather than offering new insights or solutions, making it optional for those already versed in the field. Decent charts worth skimming.

item.title: Anthropic just released the smallest and fastest Claude 3 model [ ~ ]
item.description: By offering a model that is both smaller and faster, Anthropic addresses key barriers to AI adoption, such as computational requirements and cost. But we already knew this one was coming.

item.title: Databricks invests in Mistral and brings its AI models to data intelligence platform [ ~ ]
item.description: Mistral is getting around these days. Good for them and good to note if you're using or considering Databricks, but not an essential read.

item.title: John Holland Embraces Generative AI to Enhance the Productivity of Its Workforce [ ! ]
item.description: John Holland's application of generative AI, including a custom version of ChatGPT developed in partnership with Microsoft, is an essential case study. It illustrates effective AI integration within a traditionally non-tech industry (construction), offering concrete productivity gains. Shows practical application, measurable outcomes, and the potential for replicating such success in other sectors.

item.title: Nvidia launches NIM to make it smoother to deploy AI models into production [ ! ]
item.description: These three articles stem from announcements at Nvidia's event this week. They collectively represent a significant leap forward in AI hardware and integration capabilities, highlighted by NVIDIA's announcement of the Blackwell B200 GPU as the "world's most powerful chip" for AI. Additionally, NVIDIA's enlistment of top names in humanoid robotics for its new AI platform, GR00T, indicates a substantial move towards enhancing robotic capabilities with advanced AI. These developments are crucial for anyone involved in AI, robotics, or their applications across industries.

item.title: TacticAI: an AI assistant for football tactics [ * ]
item.description: The introduction of TacticAI by Google DeepMind and Liverpool FC applies a combo of types of AI within sports analytics. It predicts the outcomes of football tactics, such as corner kicks, underscoring the growing impact of AI on sports strategy. And, importantly, it demonstrates the technology's ability to simulate scenarios and recommend strategies based on predictive analysis, demonstrating the broader applicability of AI in analyzing complex, dynamic systems across different sectors.

item.title: Siemens to deepen collaboration with NVIDIA related to generative AI for immersive real-time visualization [ * ]
item.description: This partnership highlights significant advancements in manufacturing and design processes through the integration of NVIDIA's Omniverse and Siemens' digital twin technology. It exemplifies the industrial sector's ongoing evolution towards more AI-integrated operations, marking it as an important development in the field of AI and manufacturing.

item.title: 16 Changes to the Way Enterprises Are Building and Buying Generative AI [ ! ]
item.description: This article highlights significant trends, such as the rapid deployment of AI models and the integration of AI into core IT budgets, which are essential for AI leaders to understand. The detailed survey and visualizations offered in the article make it a vital resource for supporting AI leaders' budget requests.

item.title: Introducing SceneScript, a novel approach for 3D scene reconstruction [ * ]
item.description: Meta's development of SceneScript marks a significant advancement in 3D scene reconstruction, leveraging AI to understand and interact with virtual environments more efficiently. The open-source nature of the project and its application in enhancing AR glasses and especially robotics makes it a crucial development for the future of virtual interaction and machine perception.

item.title: Improve performance and reduce cost with fractional H100 GPUs [ ~ ]
item.description: Although fractional H100 GPUs (charged by the minute) offered by Baseten present a cost-effective solution for businesses needing high computational power temporarily, the broader impact on the market and its adoption remains uncertain.

item.title: NHS AI test spots tiny cancers missed by doctors [ ~ ]
item.description: The NHS's AI model for spotting tiny cancers that were previously missed by doctors illustrates the potential for AI to enhance diagnostic accuracy in healthcare and raise the bar on the standard of care. However, this isn't a new use case so we consider this an optional read.

item.title: Improving LLM performance with agentic behavior [ ~ ]
item.description: AI heavyweight Andrew Ng explains how to create agentic behavior to improve LLM outcomes. Important to know but his instructions are a bit high level so marking this as optional.

item.title: Microsoft's first AI PCs are the Surface Pro 10 and Surface Laptop 6 for businesses [ * ]
item.description: Microsoft's strategic move to integrate AI capabilities directly into personal hardware (via neural processing units) through the Surface Pro 10 and Surface Laptop 6 shows the company's move to vertically integrate down to the user. More strategic brilliance from Nadella.

item.title: Introducing the 01 Developer Preview [ ! ]
item.description: The 01 device from Open Interpreter represents a super cool approach to integrating intelligence across various environments, offering open-source hardware and software that can significantly accelerate innovation in voice-activated control and automation. Its potential for widespread application and impact, encouragement for open innovation and the fact that AI leaders may have to deal with employees bringing this into the enterprise make this essential. (Our John Sviokla ordered one so review forthcoming!)

item.title: Accenture's Generative AI Revenue Surpasses All VC-Backed Startups Combined [ * ]
item.description: While our experience working at major consulting firms leads us to believe some of the reported $1B in GenAI work reported is reclassification of current work/resources, this article offers AI leaders a good adoption proof point when asking for budget and resources for GenAI.

item.title: RAFT: Adapting Language Model to Domain Specific RAG [ * ]
item.description: This piece introduces an approach combining retrieval augmentation (RAG) with fine-tuning techniques to enhance the applicability and efficiency of language models in specific domains. It is particularly relevant for technical teams looking to leverage the latest advancements in AI to improve model performance and applicability. For AI leaders, understanding and potentially adopting RAFT could lead to significant improvements in AI-driven projects.

item.title: KPMG Using Generative AI To Enhance Capabilities Of Digital Gateway For Tax [ ~ ]
item.description: A GenAI upgrade to KPMG's existing offering that is hopefully a lot better than what we saw from some other tax assistance platforms like TurboTax. If you're a user, let us know what you think of this one!

item.title: Tennessee becomes the first US state to protect musicians from the threat of AI [ * ]
item.description: New "Elvis Act" safeguards the intellectual property rights of musicians (including use of their voice) in the face of advancing AI technologies. Monitoring progress on various state and federal acts around IP issues as well as seeing how they later hold up in court is critical.

item.title: Financial Times tests an AI chatbot trained on decades of its own articles [ ~ ]
item.description: The Financial Times' pilot with 500 FT Pro users is a nice example of an AI chatbot for enhancing user engagement, but is becoming common low-hanging fruit, making this optional news.

item.title: Stability AI CEO resigns to pursue decentralized AI [ ~ ]
item.description: This latest departure of a key executive comes after several other resignations of critical employees in recent weeks as Stability struggles to generate revenue to support its AI decentralization ambitions. One to watch for those leaning on Stability offerings.

item.title: The Unbundling of ChatGPT [ * ]
item.description: While we know GenAI solutions are increasingly becoming verticalized, the article is worth a read and features a nice chart of some of the role-specific GenAI tools out there. Also features a graph that shows ChatGPT hasn't acquired new users in a while to help prove the point.

item.title: Pentagon Tested Generative AI to Draft Supply Plans in Latest GIDE 9 Wargame [ ~ ]
item.description: This experiment underscores the broader implications of AI in enhancing decision-making processes and operational efficiencies in complex, dynamic environments but not an essential read or groundbreaking use case.

item.title: New Report Highlights Critical Gap Between Employees and Executives Around Generative AI Leadership Readiness [ ~ ]
item.description: This report from Udemy just repeats a call to action for educational initiatives rather than presenting new developments in AI technology or applications (and of course, markets their ability to provide that education).

item.title: Is Your Company's Data Ready for Generative AI? [ * ]
item.description: This article by the prolific Tom Davenport delves into the readiness of companies' data for leveraging generative AI technologies. Through survey data, it paints a picture of the current state, where (unsurprisingly) most Chief Data Officers find themselves unprepared for the demands of generative AI. Some helpful figures for benchmarking and Tom always bring a thoughtful approach so worth a quick read.

item.title: New MLPerf Inference Benchmark Results Highlight the Rapid Growth of Generative AI Models [ ~ ]
item.description: While these benchmarks are critical for developers and researchers focusing on optimizing AI model performance, the technical nature and specific focus of the benchmarks might limit their immediate relevance to a broader audience. A nothing burger.

item.title: Hume AI Raises $50M After Building the Most Realistic Generative AI Chat Experience Yet [ * ]
item.description: While the development of a chatbot with empathy and emotional intelligence is promising for the future of AI chatbots in sectors like healthcare this is a funding announcement. However, you can follow the link to play with the model so we're putting this as important as it's worth giving it a go.

item.title: Amazon Doubles Down on Anthropic, Completing its Planned $4B Investment [ * ]
item.description: Amazon finished out their initial investment - chump change for them so while this is a nice vote of confidence, don't read too much into it. Remember what happened with Inflection.

item.title: Databricks Launches DBRX, Challenging Big Tech in the Open Source AI Race [ * ]
item.description: Databricks seems to constantly make the news these days with strategic moves and growth. They're now venturing into the competitive arena of open-source large language models with DBRX and claim it has GPT-4 level performance with more efficiency. They're becoming a major player.

item.title: Artificial intelligence boosts super-resolution microscopy [ ~ ]
item.description: Interesting to see a new spin on diffusion for image generation, what they call a Conditional Variational Diffusion Model (CVDM), but this isn't immediately relevant to the AI leader.

item.title: Microsoft launches new Azure AI tools to cut out LLM safety and reliability risks [ * ]
item.description: We usually don't rate announcements of products that are not yet available as important. But given the prevalence of Microsoft in the enterprise and the issues this will reportedly address - hallucinations, prompt injection attacks and more - we want AI leaders to know this is coming.

item.title: Congress bans staff use of Microsoft's AI Copilot [ * ]
item.description: Showcases the government's rightfully cautious stance towards integrating GenAI tools within its operations, emphasizing security and privacy concerns.

item.title: OpenAI and Microsoft Plan $100 Billion AI 'Stargate' [ ~ ]
item.description: It will be interesting to see if AI's power couple pull off this planned build of a mega-AI data center, but it's only in the planning stages at this point.

item.title: How Stability AI's Founder Tanked His Billion-Dollar Startup [ ~ ]
item.description: This long, well-researched story is rich in details about the operational and managerial missteps leading to Stability AI's challenges.

item.title: Generative AI to quantify uncertainty in weather forecasting [ ~ ]
item.description: Another example of Google's AI research prowess - and we welcome better weather forecasts - but not essential news for the AI leader.

item.title: OpenAI built a voice cloning tool, but you can't use it... yet [ ~ ]
item.description: Another announcement from OpenAI about a capability that no one can use yet. Plus other providers like ElevenLabs already offer this.

item.title: NYC's AI Chatbot Tells Businesses to Break the Law [ ~ ]
item.description: Another cautionary tale about putting GenAI tools out in the wild without proper tuning and guardrails.

item.title: The Unreasonable Ineffectiveness of the Deeper Layers [ ~ ]
item.description: Authors report improving upon well-established pruning techniques. May be good fodder for engineers looking for new tricks, but not an essential read for the AI executive.

item.title: It's for Real: Generative AI Takes Hold in Insurance Distribution [ ~ ]
item.description: We know Insurance is an industry 'in the crucible' based on our WINS framework and hoped this article would provide some fresh insights. But there's not much new info here, and we didn't necessarily agree with the analysis provided in the charts, so giving this one an optional rating.

item.title: Generative AI: The next S-curve for the semiconductor industry? [ ~ ]
item.description: Despite presenting forward-looking insights into the potential B2B and B2C GenAI growth areas that will drive semi demand, speculative assumptions in the analysis and a slog of a read led to its optional rating. Some interesting points if you can hang in there with it, but it doesn't provide a solid enough foundation for immediate action or decision-making.

item.title: Yum Brands Doubles Tech Spending, Expands Use of Generative AI [ * ]
item.description: Yum Brands has a pretty comprehensive strategy for applying GenAI across its operations and is putting $21M (double last year's spend) into digital innovation this year. Core areas of its business are being targeted. This is another good article to have in your back pocket when trying to get budget for GenAI or facing skepticism over its value. But Yum appears to have no GenAI apps in production yet, preventing us from elevating this to an essential read.

item.title: Apple researchers develop AI that can 'see' and understand screen context [ ~ ]
item.description: Yet again, Apple in the news around GenAI, but not for announcing any GenAI products. This research is geared toward improving context to help them (eventually) create a good experience when using GenAI on your iPhone. Interesting, but not a critical read.

item.title: For Data-Guzzling AI Companies, the Internet Is Too Small [ * ]
item.description: We had a lively discussion around this one (starts around minute 26:00 in our morning briefing). It highlights the challenge of finding new data sources to improve the biggest of models any further given they've hoovered the entire internet, including many (but not all) video transcripts. As you've heard many times before, AI leaders, your company's data is extremely valuable. Are you using it to its full potential? You need to be.

item.title: Gen-AI Search Engine Perplexity Has a Plan to Sell Ads [ * ]
item.description: Search is changing - this is essential for a CMO but only important from an awareness perspective for the AI leader. You to be informed as to all the ways GenAI is changing the game in long-standing industry norms. Recall this startup also focused in this area.

item.title: Many-shot Jailbreaking [ * ]
item.description: Anthropic found this issue and kindly alerted other LLM providers to it. They've mitigated it in their models (though not to 100%) but we don't know if other providers have. Also, if you're building your own model, you need to be aware of this and take steps to combat it as well.

item.title: Luminance's Generative AI-for-law raises $40M Series B [ ~ ]
item.description: Despite acknowledging Luminance's achievement and healthy competition for Harvey, we see this as primarily a sector-specific development. It was noted that while the funding signifies growth in legal tech AI, it represents a trend rather than a breakthrough, making it of optional interest to those not directly involved in legal AI.

item.title: Hailo lands $120 million to keep battling Nvidia as most AI chip startups struggle [ ~ ]
item.description: Although Hailo's successful fundraising marks its significance in the AI chip industry and the move toward compute at the edge, the group consensus leaned towards this news being optional. They seem to be gaining traction but Nvidia and other major players still rule the roost.

item.title: WHO Unveils a Digital Health Promoter Harnessing Generative AI for Public Health [ * ]
item.description: This development was considered important due to WHO's significant role in global health and the potential impact of introducing an AI-driven assistant like this one (named SARAH) to serve the historically underserved. This is a major, cautious organization jumping into the GenAI mix. And our tests show the tool is quite good, despite a little latency and repetitiveness.

item.title: Nature Communications Publishes Zapata AI Research on Generative AI for Optimization [ ~ ]
item.description: While the findings demonstrate the potential for quantum modeling to outperform traditional methods in complex optimization problems like portfolio management, its current status as emerging research renders it an optional consideration for a broader audience. We do think we'll see more quantum+AI progress so a good weekend read if you want to geek out a bit.

item.title: AI adoption accelerates as enterprise PoCs show productivity gains [ ! ]
item.description: This article underscores the tangible benefits and productivity gains realized through GenAI adoption. Highlighting examples from 3 major companies - Webster Bank, Eli Lilly and Eaton - it highlights a lot of the best practices we've been espousing. Long but essential read with good proof points for the AI executive.

item.title: Enhancing The Forrester Experience With Generative AI [ ~ ]
item.description: A chatbot that provides on-demand info for high-tier users. What took you so long? Nothing burger.

item.title: Startup Datavolo raises over $21M to transform how generative AI models access unstructured data [ * ]
item.description: Datavolo's announcement is not necessarily significant for the capital raise, but it is for spotlighting the critical challenge of structuring your data pipeline - you'll need these types of tools because the classic ones won't cut it for routing unstructured data to GenAI.

item.title: I have a group chat with three AI friends, thanks to Nomi AI they're getting too smart [ ~ ]
item.description: Explores the evolving capabilities of AI in creating more convincing and emotionally intelligent virtual companions. Highlighting personal experiences with Nomi AI's chatbots, the discussion reflects on the broader implications for social interaction and mental health. Intriguing for its societal implications, but its immediate relevance to enterprise AI strategy and day-to-day operations is limited.

item.title: Microsoft 365's Copilot gets a GPT-4 Turbo upgrade and improved image generation [ ~ ]
item.description: The upgrade to Microsoft 365's Copilot with GPT-4 Turbo and enhanced image generation capabilities signifies a notable advancement for users already embedded in the M365 ecosystem. While it introduces more powerful models for reasoning and supports larger text prompts, along with improved daily limits for image creation, it's seen as an incremental upgrade, but good for M365 users to be aware of.

item.title: DALL-E now lets you edit images in ChatGPT [ ~ ]
item.description: Finally, in-painting comes to ChatGPT. It has been available in other popular image generation apps like Midjourney for a while. Our David DeLallo is a Midjourney power user, but says this will make him start exploring the use of ChatGPT more to create his weekly AI comic.

item.title: Google using AI to come up with search answers in UK trial [ ~ ]
item.description: Google's expansion of its AI-driven search answers into the UK is another step in Google's testing of its Search Generative Experience, which is available to beta testers (we're among them) in the US. No need to read - we've just shared the news in a nutshell for you.

item.title: Wiz uncovers security flaws at Hugging Face [ * ]
item.description: Israeli cloud security firm, Wiz, was able to access private data and models from Hugging Face users by uploading a malicious LLM. Hugging Face has patched the flaw, but this is an important reminder of the continuous need for vigilance in vetting providers. This hack was possible because Hugging Face stores all instances of models and data uploads from users in the same cloud - they, of course, aren't alone in this.

item.title: Introducing Command R+: A Scalable LLM Built for Business [ * ]
item.description: Cohere seems to be emphasizing its competitive pricing, though Command R+ is several times more expensive than Command-R (launched a few weeks ago). Of note that there's another option out there of an LLM with associated tooling.

item.title: OpenAI expands its custom model training program [ ~ ]
item.description: Good to know about some incremental improvements to OpenAI's tuning API and the scaling up of their hands-on work with customers, but not an essential read. Scattered among the technical notes, they share that Indeed and SK Telekom are using OpenAI models in applications.

item.title: JetMoE: Reaching LLaMA2 Performance with 0.1M Dollars [ * ]
item.description: A demonstration of achieving high-level AI performance with significantly reduced costs, though they compare this model's performance to Llama 2 as opposed to the most powerful models. Still, it offers hope to enterprises that it may not cost millions to build a custom model that gives you a competitive advantage.

item.title: SiMa.ai secures $70M funding to introduce a multimodal GenAI chip [ ~ ]
item.description: Our Luda Kopeikina, a venture capitalist, notes that the valuation of this firm hasn't increased in this funding round so the future for this company might not be as bright as this announcement indicates. They're SoC offering is for the edge, which could make them an interesting takeover target for Nvidia, who isn't yet playing on the edge much.

item.title: S&P Global launches groundbreaking AI benchmark for the financial industry [ * ]
item.description: We've been espousing the importance of industry-specific benchmarks for real-world AI performance. S&P Global's initiative serves as a pioneering example in the financial sector where precision, reliability and fostering trust are paramount.

item.title: How Google lost ground in the AI race [ ~ ]
item.description: Similar to the previous piece, this is well-written and captures the details on the causes of Google's well-covered AI fumbles, but is an optional read. The company's GenAI course to date makes for a good Harvard Business case study - a giant organization with duplicative projects happening in silos that faces the innovator's dilemma around their search business.

item.title: Large language models are able to downplay their cognitive abilities to fit the persona they simulate [ ~ ]
item.description: This is not a surprising feature. We know that giving GenAI chatbots a persona (eg, 'act like the most effective marketer in the world') works well. If you're not employing this technique in your prompting strategies, you should be.

item.title: How Tech Giants Cut Corners to Harvest Data for A.I. [ ~ ]
item.description: A nice piece of reporting that gets into the details of the lengths OpenAI, Google and others are going to in order to get more data to train their models. And, as we know, the legality of some of their methods are questionable. A reminder to the AI leader about how valuable your data is. Good read if you have the time, but optional.

item.title: SWE-agent turns LMs (e.g. GPT-4) into software engineering agents that can fix bugs and issues in real GitHub repositories [ ~ ]
item.description: An application that looks to compete with Devin, but demonstrates slightly less effective performance and has a clunkier UX. Expect to see many more Devin competitors emerge.

item.title: Meta will require labels on more AI-generated content [ ~ ]
item.description: Of course Meta needs to do this to look like they're trying their best in the eyes of regulators and the public, but we know tools aimed at identifying AI-generated content are not very effective so don't expect a lot of help here.

item.title: Hercules AI unveils assembly line approach for building enterprise-grade gen AI apps [ * ]
item.description: This platform looks promising for helping industries with a lot of info trapped in spreadsheets to extract it and enable LLMs to do what they do best - improve worker productivity. It also features an LLM that gets impressive coding results that surpass GPT-4 by simply fine-tuning a 7B model.

item.title: Jamie Dimon says AI may be as impactful on humanity as printing press, electricity and computers [ * ]
item.description: The headline isn't why we tagged this as important (and our John Sviokla argued it is essential). It's the information provided in Dimon's annual investor letter that we want the AI leader to absorb. JP Morgan is a tech leader among banks: 2,000 AI/ML workers, 400 apps in production, 32 data centers, and private and public clouds (though still migrating there). And Dimon says he sees AI impacting every role.

item.title: Coles turns GenAI onto 40,000 customer comments a week [ * ]
item.description: Another article that nearly made it to essential because it's a great use case. Coles is a giant supermarket chain in Australia. They're using GenAI to process the 40K customer comments they collect each month and acting on the insights at a store level. Well done!

item.title: Biocompare Announces Beta Launch of LifeSciAI, a New Generative AI Tool [ ~ ]
item.description: This supplier of products for the experimenting scientist is offering a chatbot that has knowledge of 8 million lab supplies and tons of experiments, but it's a common use case and a niche user base so we rated it optional.

item.title: Google rolls out Gemini in Android Studio for coding assistance [ ~ ]
item.description: A nothing burger. It would be news if Google DIDN'T offer a coding tool.

item.title: Stability AI brings 12B parameters to Stable LM 2 model update [ ~ ]
item.description: Great that the company is still pumping out new models despite the turmoil over there, but are AI leaders going to use models from an organization that is hanging on by a thread? Imagine trying to justify that to your CEO...

item.title: TSMC receives $6.6B to build chip factories under U.S. CHIPS and Science Act [ ~ ]
item.description: While essential for everyone as US citizens, optional read for the AI leader. Good to see the Chips Act working, and TSMC is more on track to stand up the 3 foundries they're building in Arizona than Intel - the first one is set to come online in 1H2025.

item.title: Ferret-UI: Grounded Mobile UI Understanding with Multimodal LLMs [ ~ ]
item.description: This is the paper that follows on the research announcement from a week or so ago. As we said then, of course Apple is putting effort into GenAI computing at the edge since it's where the company plays hardest.

item.title: New Federal Bill Could Require Disclosure of Songs Used in AI Training [ ~ ]
item.description: Rep. Adam Schiff introduced a bill that calls on LLM providers to reveal what music was used in their training data (nothing around other content types - industry lobbying, anyone?) but we've got some time to see if this becomes a law so nothing to see here yet.

item.title: Dairyland powers up for a generative AI edge [ ~ ]
item.description: We had high expectations for this article, hoping to see some interesting use cases from a local utility. But in the end, seems they're pretty much just using Copilot for coding and generating communications. They are using traditional AI in more impactful ways, though, so maybe more to come on the GenAI front soon.

item.title: Intel Unleashes Enterprise AI with Gaudi 3, AI Open Systems Strategy and New Customer Wins [ * ]
item.description: Intel is still a few years behind Nvidia, but competition is needed in this space to meet demand and bring prices down so good to see Intel keeping at it.

item.title: Google Cloud Next 2024: Everything announced so far [ ! ]
item.description: It may be a cloud event but AI is taking center stage. A new video generation tool in Workspace, a revamped image generation tool in the developer kit, and an agent builder were among the announced products. Nothing edgy - mostly their versions of tools already available from others. But Workspace has a huge user base and Google is 3rd in cloud, so worth knowing about.

item.title: AMD launches second-generation Versal chips to make AI faster at the edge [ ~ ]
item.description: This is an upgrade to an existing chip - feels like a 'me too' announcement on the day of Intel's. Important to know if you're a customer but not worth reading the article otherwise.

item.title: Beyond Transformers: Symbolica launches with $33M to change the AI industry with symbolic models [ ~ ]
item.description: Early days for this company that plans to combine symbolic AI, which has been worked on for decades, with deep learning to produce models and applications that are interpretable. John Sviokla and Tim Andrews engaged in a spirited (albeit geeky) discussion about when and whether LLMs could become interpretable which is worth watching in the recording or today's briefing, but Symbolica doesn't plan to release anything until 2025 so this is one to watch, but optional for now.

item.title: Poe introduces a price-per-message revenue model for AI bot creators [ * ]
item.description: Quora seems to have beaten OpenAI to the punch in providing a way for creators to monetize the bots they create using a revenue model similar to app stores. This is for bots developed on any platform as long as they integrate with Quora's Poe AI. Increasingly tough to understand why Quora's CEO still sits on OpenAI's board...

item.title: Ask your assets anything: State Street's generative AI lets investors chat with their data [ ~ ]
item.description: This piece of news almost made it to important. Custody is a boring but critical area of global finance. And State Street is one of a handful of banks that collectively serve as the 'keeper' of about 90% of assets. The company is building a chatbot for custody customers to interact with as well as a bot for a broader group of customers to more easily interact with their research. We would have rated this as Important if the bots were already available but they aren't just yet.

item.title: Intercom's new Fin AI Copilot gives customer service agents their personal AI assistant [ ~ ]
item.description: We know customer service is a prime use case, and this is a platform for building your own GenAI-powered application. But organizations are doing just fine building these already so not sure this will get a ton of traction.

item.title: Mistral AI drops new 'mixture of experts' model with a torrent link [ ~ ]
item.description: We may elevate this to important once we start to learn how the models perform, but Mistral's minimalist method of announcing releases makes it tough for us to assess this development for the moment. We do know this is a talented bunch so we expect good things!

item.title: OpenEQA: From word models to world models [ ! ]
item.description: Meta released a benchmark to help model developers assess how their models do with establishing a representation of the world, which is essential for progressing the abilities of AI and robots. LLMs aren't very good at this--the latest version of GPT-4 does best based on Meta's analysis (full results provided in the article). The benchmark itself isn't necessarily essential but spurring research in this area is.

item.title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models? [ ~ ]
item.description: Another benchmark. This one confirms what many of us experience - LLMs don't perform as well in their purported context windows as their developers claim. GPT-4 does best. Could be a more useful benchmark than some existing ones. Put it on your radar but might not be worth the long read.

item.title: European car manufacturer will pilot Sanctuary AI's humanoid robot [ ~ ]
item.description: BMW, Mercedes, Jaguar and others have committed to testing this robot. Great to see robotics moving forward, but let's see how these pilots pan out before we elevate this to important or essential.

item.title: The Weather Channel's parent company has a new AI tool to make hyperlocal weather videos [ ~ ]
item.description: Helpful for meteorologists, but the use case doesn't feature any novelties so parking this one in the optional spot.

item.title: NTT Research unveils AI model, sustainable path for AI, and better distributed data centers [ * ]
item.description: Three major announcements of note here: (1) they're releasing a model they claim does better than GPT-4 on analyzing inputs that contain graphics and text , (2) they propose a paradigm for distributed data centers that can improve their energy efficiency, and (3) they announce a partnership with Harvard to advance knowledge about the brain which would benefit AI development and human understanding. Research, but all critical areas.

item.title: Snowflake Copilot, a Mistral Large-powered AI assistant, launches in public preview [ ~ ]
item.description: Snowflake now enables natural-language prompts that translate into technical SQL queries. Nice feature, but no need to read the article.

item.title: Microsoft is working on sound recognition AI technologies capable of detecting natural disasters [ * ]
item.description: While this is only the announcement of Microsoft's filing of a patent in this area, 'AI as ears' will open up a host of new use cases. Here, Microsoft is patenting a technology that better senses sounds amid background noise. Important to start thinking about how you might be able to use this capability.

item.title: Introducing Rerank 3: A New Foundation Model for Efficient Enterprise Search & Retrieval [ * ]
item.description: The introduction of Rerank 3 by Cohere signals important advancements in cost efficiency and performance in enterprise search solutions.

item.title: The rise of the chief AI officer [ * ]
item.description: There's a significant focus on the necessity of having dedicated AI leadership to navigate the complex legal, ethical, and operational challenges.

item.title: The Worst Part of a Wall Street Career May Be Coming to an End [ * ]
item.description: Banks leaders say that AI could soon enable them to cut down on junior analyst hires by a whopping two-thirds. Implications are huge for organizations.

item.title: Apple plans Mac line overhaul with AI-focused M4 chips, Bloomberg News reports [ ~ ]
item.description: Yet again, Apple making news for something forthcoming but not yet available. Even when this chip drops, it's just an upgrade.

item.title: Generative AI is coming for healthcare, and not everyone's thrilled [ * ]
item.description: Put aside the fear-mongering headline. The article provides a good list of use cases that healthcare providers are exploring.

item.title: British DARPA' to build AI gatekeepers for 'quantitative safety guarantees [ ~ ]
item.description: Certifications like the one this group is working on are welcomed, but this is still in the works.

item.title: Former Google DeepMind researchers launch AI-powered music creation app Udio [ ~ ]
item.description: We knew this was coming and now it's here. Used in marketing and entertainment, but not an essential read.

item.title: 2024 AI Index Report [ ! ]
item.description: This annual report from Stanford University is a comprehensive and valuable resource on AI's current state.

item.title: Cohere Compass Private Beta: A New Multi-Aspect Embedding Model [ * ]
item.description: Offers a new approach to embedding models that could improve enterprise data systems management.

item.title: A.I. Has a Measurement Problem [ * ]
item.description: We need reliable and standard ways to evaluate and compare model performance.

item.title: Reka Core, Flash, and Edge: A Series of Powerful Multimodal Language Models [ * ]
item.description: Competitive offering from a small but well-funded group in Singapore with former Google Brain and DeepMind founders is notable.

item.title: OpenAI's Altman pitches ChatGPT Enterprise to large firms, including some Microsoft customers [ ~ ]
item.description: Unsurprising continued coopetition at play with no compelling reason to engage OpenAI directly.

item.title: Adobe Premiere Pro is getting generative AI video tools - and hopefully OpenAI's Sora [ ~ ]
item.description: The capability isn't yet available, and the integration of Sora isn't even certain.

item.title: ArenaX Labs launches ARC AI game infrastructure and SAI research platform [ ~ ]
item.description: Cool development in gaming but not of note to the AI leader.

item.title: C6 Bank accelerates innovation using generative AI with AWS [ * ]
item.description: The use cases this major Brazilian bank backed by JP Morgan is implementing are low-hanging fruit (coding and customer service), but that's why we're flagging. These use cases are becoming table stakes so if you're not already at least testing them, you're falling behind.

item.title: Microsoft Makes High-Stakes Play in Tech Cold War With Emirati A.I. Deal [ * ]
item.description: Microsoft's investment into G42 has been orchestrated by the US government as a way to get companies in the Middle East more aligned to the US as opposed to China. While this is important from a geopolitical perspective, it's also yet another proof point for the AI leader that GenAI is truly powerful - our government is moving swiftly and decisively to position the US as a global AI powerhouse.

item.title: Pegasystems offers every worker access to a personalized, generative AI-powered coach [ * ]
item.description: This is another article we're flagging as a source of GenAI use case ideas. This low-code software provider is using GenAI internally in interesting ways - it integrates GenAI into an individual's workflow in a personalized way so that it gives advice to a sales or back-office worker in the course of their work.

item.title: Zendesk users get generative AI infusion for customer service [ * ]
item.description: While it's not surprising that a customer service software provider would integrate GenAI into it offering, the company includes some other nice features that provide ideas for any organization. The tool helps predict staffing levels and prioritizes an agent's work in addition to providing the agent with the best answers to customer issues.

item.title: Nvidia expands Ampere-based GPUs for AI design and productivity apps [ * ]
item.description: Nvidia is everywhere - including at the edge. This will enable laptops to run AI faster.

item.title: Cheaper, Better, Faster, Stronger [ * ]
item.description: In this article, Mistral provides information on the 8X22B open source model it released last week. The highlights are that it covers 5 languages, offers native function-calling capability, and claims to have better performance-to-cost ratio than its nearest competitors, Llama 2 and Cohere's Command models.

item.title: 12 companies that rolled out internal AI tools for employees [ * ]
item.description: The article shares an overview of GenAI-powered general knowledge and HR assistance tools used by both big (PwC, Walmart) and smaller firms (Pipefy). Easy read and a good scan of the types of tools that are becoming commonplace in many organizations. Worth a few minutes of your time.

item.title: BigPanda launches generative AI tool designed specifically for ITOps [ * ]
item.description: While this functionality doesn't look extremely sophisticated, any help here is welcomed, and the AI leaders who also head up IT should take note that this functionality will be coming to the platform of your choice soon.

item.title: Logitech wants you to press its new AI button [ * ]
item.description: Let's be clear - this isn't important for the release of the $49.99 mouse itself. What's important is the fact that we're moving toward a world where we'll all have a physical 'easy button' that activates an assistant to help us do many everyday tasks (remember that Microsoft is installing one on keyboards as well).

item.title: Thomson Reuters unveils CoCounsel, leveraging generative AI for legal professionals [ ! ]
item.description: Big name with a lot of data entering an increasingly crowded space, but one where Harvey has maintained its dominance to date. A formidable competitor has arrived. The economics for law firms and everyone who leans on them are changing fast. For AI leaders, this is a reminder that if your company is in an industry in the crucible according to our WINS framework, you have little time to lose.

item.title: Generative AI in manufacturing - out of the old, emerges the new [ * ]
item.description: Industrial giant Bosch details how they're creating synthetic data to enable GenAI-powered quality assurance. The company noted that it has so few defects in its products, that it doesn't have enough error-ridden product images to train the system - a little self-promo never hurts. This is a great use case.

item.title: Meta launches Llama 3 [ ! ]
item.description: This isn't an "another model, another day" type of announcement. Besides already shooting to the top of the open-source model leaderboard on performance, Llama 3 is now heavily integrated into all of Meta's social channels, enabling search, image generation, animations and more right in its apps. The image generation capability is particularly impressive - so fast that the images generate as you type in your "order." Llama 3 still doesn't hold a candle to the top closed source models but the next version of it due out in the summer sounds like it might...

item.title: ChatGPT is coming to Nothing's earbuds [ ~ ]
item.description: The name of the company (which creates mobile phones - anyone actually have one?) says it all about this nonessential development.

item.title: Meet Lingo-2, a groundbreaking AI model that navigates roads and narrates its journey [ * ]
item.description: London-based autonomous driving tech provider Wayve released this second version of its multi-modal model that can share what it's doing as it maneuvers (so far, only in simulation environments). Multimodal is the future so this is of note, but the development of this model is not yet essential given where we are with autonomous vehicles.

item.title: Honeywell exec reveals plan to deliver $100 million in value with generative AI: "Just getting started" [ * ]
item.description: While this isn't a significant amount of value generation for a $90B+ company, Honeywell shares info about its organizational GenAI strategy here that offers some tips / validation for the AI leaders' approach.

item.title: Two-thirds of top 20 pharmas have banned ChatGPT-and many in life sci call AI 'overrated,' survey finds [ ~ ]
item.description: This click-bate got our John Sviokla fired up on an early Monday morning.
